G.engine: No. Every round, round 1 included, runs Sway, then the whole adversary turn, then Cards (in round 1 that is the opening deal). The game opens with the adversary's turn.

G.engine: In the Corrupt step, each agent next to a target city that is not itself a target moves onto it (the players choose if it is next to several), so the city holds 3. At the baseline difficulty 0 a city needs 4, so nothing else happens. From level 1 a city needs 3, so it corrupts: the adversary cube replaces any owner cube, the agents go back to the supply, any node there is destroyed (protections apply), player ambassadors there are removed and markers come off. An agent arriving on an ambassador cancels one, one for one.
G.evidence: adversary.rs:1369-1420 corrupt_sites (converge, then held >= n corrupts; held adds a city's markers); plan.rs:135-170 converge (agents on a target stay; moves cross borders); adversary.rs:1348-1366 corrupt_n with corrupt_cut from level 1 (baseline.json:54 difficulty 0, :61 corrupt_at 4, :66-72 cut [1,1,1,0] at 1); adversary.rs:1292-1327 corrupt_hex; adversary.rs:1423-1435 converge_one cancels an ambassador.

G.engine: Nothing happens at once. In the adversary turn's natural corruption step (or earlier in a Corrupt nodes line), a hex with a player's node and 2 agents loses the node. The agents go to the supply and the protection order applies: Shelter does not cover the adversary turn, then the owner may spend a hardening token or shield, their own ambassador, or Aegis. Sanctuary keeps the node. A destroyed node leaves a corruption marker unless the hex is already tainted, and nothing else on the hex changes.
G.evidence: adversary.rs:1440-1466 natural_corruption (City, Station, Factory, then Node at corrupt_n Node=2, no cut: op.rs:263-270 Node index 5 past cut list); adversary.rs:1330-1345 corrupt_node (agents removed, destroy_piece unless CorruptionShield); destroy.rs:73-120 guards; node.rs:198-202 marker; board/mod.rs:228-231 and 517+ Shelter flag lasts only this round to cleanup.

G.engine: The agent and one ambassador are both removed, one for one, and the agent goes back to the adversary's supply. With several players' ambassadors there, the team chooses whose (the engine asks seat 0 for the team, which matches 'if you can't agree, the first player decides').
G.evidence: board/ambassadors.rs:35-50 agent_cancels (several seats: choose_loss(0, ...)); adversary.rs:1207-1215 arrive returns the agent to supply.

G.engine: It costs 1 ambassador from your supply, which is used up. It removes up to 3 agents one at a time from any hexes in your reach (one hex or several, and you may stop early), and places nothing. Like any standard action you can repeat it as often as you can pay.

G.engine: Claim costs 6 ambassadors: 5 for a city plus 1 for the agent. Your own ambassadors on the city pay first (1 here), and your supply pays the other 5. The agent is removed and your cube goes on. The city must be in your reach and not under embargo. (In play an ambassador and an agent can't normally share a hex, since they cancel on contact.)

G.engine: In growth, after the income step and extra drones, every city (blocked or not) with a free industrial zone next to it (no factory, station or land corruption) builds a factory there, every round. A player's city builds its owner's factory on a zone the owner chooses, and a corrupted city builds the adversary's next to an agent where it can.

G.engine: The node is at risk only if the factory itself is destroyed; if the factory is saved, the node is untouched. Shelter in that country stops both automatically. Otherwise you, the node's owner, choose to spend a hardening token or shield on the hex, your own ambassador there, or Aegis Doctrine, or nothing. Drones only guard against adversary troops.

A firewalled or prohibited site's share stays in the supply.

V.engine: 'Deploy' is the engine's word for a Muster (an event's, a project's, or the Protector landing). Each troop lands on the country's lowest-numbered factory (any owner); with no factory, its lowest-numbered city. If that hex holds the Protector's node (Wall), the troop stays in the supply and doesn't move on to another site. From level 2 the board's difficulty line adds 1 troop.

V.book_fault: The rulebook never uses the word 'Deploy' (it says Muster); the reader mapped it correctly, and §6 'A blocked landing stays in the supply' states the Wall case.

Each of its 2 steps: remove an ambassador on its hex, else strike a player-owned (uncorrupted) research station or factory on or next to it and be used up, else move one hex toward the nearest such target. Nodes are a target only from stage 4 (troop_node 4), which the 3-stage deck never reaches, so in practice never.
